newsitem.title: USA: Time Warner's cable cash a pleasant surprise.
newsitem.headline: Time Warner's cable cash a pleasant surprise.

text.p: A surprise showing by Time Warner Inc's cable television networks provided a strong cash injection in the second quarter and boosted the entertainment giant's overall performance.
"The (cash flow) numbers were great, and above our estimates," said Jessica Reif Cohen, an analyst at Merrill Lynch. "All divisions looked very strong."
Time Warner's net loss fell to $49 million from $110 million, including an extraordinary loss of $9 million, a year ago.
The closely watched EBITDA -- earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization -- or cash flow total rose to $1.31 billion from $1.03 billion for the period.
Analysts said they were surprised by the strength of the company's cable television networks, such as HBO, CNN, TNT, TBS, and the Cartoon Network.

"The surprise is the ongoing strength at Turner," said Chris Dixon at PaineWebber. "This is really a confirmation of the strategy...to use the branded networks to drive new sources of revenues and find outlets for their entertainment production."
Cash flow at its TBS networks jumped 41 percent to $186 million from a pro forma $132 million. Its HBO operation posted cash flow of $103 million versus $87 million.
Cohen said the cable news networks, suffering recently from ratings weakness, had double-digit cash flow gains.
The company said gains in both advertising and subscriber revenues drove the overall increases.

The Warner film unit posted a record $155 million in cash flow, up 10 percent. TBS filmed entertainment business, helped by the movie, "Austin Powers: International Man of Mystery," had cash flow of $31 million versus negative $21 million.
Analysts said Warner Music, which saw a decline in cash flow, was suffering from weak sales in a poor retail climate.

Its music business was hurt by a dearth of big-selling artists. "There's a lack of new artists," said Gary Farber at NatWest Securities. "International, which has carried the ball, has slowed down a little. They are not a market leader in a lot of overseas markets."
The cable systems kicked in a record combined $554 million in cash flow versus $494 million. Its cable operation has about 12.4 million cable subscribers.

Debt remains an overall drag on profits. "I don't think there was ever a question of whether this was a solid business, and that they could put up excellent growth numbers," said David Doft at Furman Selz. "But there's still a lot of debt on the balance sheet."
Analysts said the company could generate more than $5 billion in cash flow this year, with the cable networks kicking in about $1 billion, including HBO.
The company spent about $303 million in the quarter to cover interest and other payments. Analysts expect interest payments to total $1 billion for the year.
Analysts said the company remained under pressure to sell some of its cable systems and focus on entertainment. "Simpler would be better for the stock," said Doft.
Nonetheless, in late morning trading investors cheered the results. Shares gained 2-5/16 to 47-5/8.
